assumptions: 'Giant functions' means stacks over 30 statements or 3 levels of nesting (template default), not a line count
'No tests' means workflow/unit tests on endpoints, as CHG-001 checks; functions are not required to have tests in this plan
The recipe's 'legacy' tag should not be applied to existing objects without the owner's say-so
Advisory enforcement is the right default for a first rollout
workspace_names_used: acme_sync_shipping_rates (82-line function, largest stack; used as an example in the reply)
acme_get_tracking (has try_catch; example of the existing pattern)
confusions: Recipe 'Keep code easy to review' lists 'functions say what they do' under extra rules, but the rule's params are given as a JSON example only; I wrote the params myself from the recipe text (min_length 20).

Template LOG-010 summary says 'every external request sits inside a try block', but its only rule checks api.request; the limits text lists the other statements to add. Did not widen, so the summary and the rule disagree in scope.

CONV-040 limits text says on blocking policies a change over the limit is blocked even when it shrinks it, and suggests except_tags for legacy objects; it is not clear whether advisory rollout is the right default for this recipe, so I chose advisory.
The recipe's build step adds a 'legacy' tag to existing objects as part of the plan, which is an exemption of the rule; the guidance does not say when that is appropriate, so I left it to the owner.
wished_for: A recipe variant without the legacy-tag build step, or a note saying to apply it only after the owner names the objects
Parameter examples for template rules whose 'examples' field is empty (CONV-040, PERF-001) so the fill is not guessed
A template for a function-level test rule (every function has a test); CHG-001 covers endpoints only
why_confidence: The six policies parse and the dry run reports them cleanly, and the checks match the template rules. But the ask is about behaviour (stop breaking prod), and the policies are advisory and only read stored definitions. They flag missing try_catch on api.request, missing workflow tests, long stacks, leftover code, unpaged reads and undescribed functions. They do not stop a bad merge, check review, or cover other outbound calls. I have not run xano policy evaluate, so predicted findings are unverified.
